about: The pinned-sha eval-run corpus (F2 / backlog E11, R-PIPE-1). One entry per reusable target: the repo URL, the exact sha every recorded run graded, the structural scope, and the local reusable clone. A batch is reproducible from this file alone - re-clone the repo, check out the sha, point clonePath at it, and scripts/eval-run.mjs refuses to grade anything that is not at the pin.

conventions.sha: The full 40-char sha. The eval-runs record cites the short form; the runner accepts a short pin as a prefix match.
conventions.scope: The structural kind of the target: plugin (one plugin root), component (one skill directory), collection (many skill directories with no plugin manifest), marketplace-by-hand (many plugins graded one at a time, since the gate has no marketplace scope), index (a curation list that ships no components on disk, so nothing is gradeable - kept pinned because the negative result is itself corpus evidence). The RUN scope recorded in eval-runs.md comes from the evaluator's own detection, not from this field.
conventions.clonePath: A local reusable clone, forward-slash normalized. Machine-specific by nature: re-point it after cloning elsewhere. The runner never writes into a clone.
conventions.subpath: The graded path inside the clone, or null for the clone root. Overridable per run with --subpath.
conventions.profile: The gate profile past runs used for this target. Third-party targets are graded under plain-plugin so house conventions do not score against them.

targets.notes: Batch 1 anchor (the official Anthropic set). Runs R3 and R5 graded single skills in component scope: --subpath skills/mcp-builder and --subpath skills/pdf. The clone root itself grades as a plugin-shaped collection (a skills/ tree with no library.json).

Batch 2 anchor. 86 skills, no enumerating manifest: the collection-scale target that set the advisory sampling protocol (run R6 deep-read 13 of 86 for ~77k tokens). 0 errors / 0 warnings under plain-plugin.

Batch 2 anchor and the pipeline's smoke target. 49 skills, a full plugin with a marketplace catalog; the defect-rich member of the corpus (11 errors / 12 warnings under plain-plugin at this pin), which is why run R7 set the measured advisory ceiling and why reading 8 (verify before calibrate) came from it.

Batch 2 anchor and the same-target model triple (R8/R9/R10/R11 all graded pm-toolkit). A 9-plugin marketplace: the gate has no marketplace scope, so each plugin is graded on its own by passing --subpath (pm-ai-shipping, pm-data-analytics, pm-execution, pm-go-to-market, pm-market-research, pm-marketing-growth, pm-product-discovery, pm-product-strategy, pm-toolkit). All nine were 0 errors / 0 warnings under plain-plugin at this pin.

Batch 3 anchor and the release-3 marketplace ground truth: a 2-member marketplace (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json registers terminal-skills at ./claude-plugin and seog at ./plugins/seog), each member shipping exactly ONE skill and an MCP server, sitting on a 1016-skill root skills/ tree that neither member enumerates. Graded three ways at this pin: the clone root, --subpath claude-plugin, --subpath plugins/seog. Cross-agent by documentation (the README instructs Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor installs) but ships no Codex manifest anywhere in the tree; the only structural trace is an agents: [...] frontmatter key on 136 of the 1016 skills, so the cross-agent claim is prose plus a partial convention, not a native manifest.

NOT GRADEABLE at this pin, deliberately kept: the whole repository is one 457-line README.md that links out to 218 skills hosted elsewhere. Zero SKILL.md, zero manifests, zero component directories on disk. The runner refuses it with code not-gradeable, which is the correct outcome and the reason the entry is worth pinning. Because a refusal throws, `--all` aborts the whole batch when it reaches this entry: name targets explicitly instead.

Batch 3 anchor and the record's first non-English corpus: 349 skills under skills/, every description written in French. Also the corpus's first whole-tree duplication case - each skill exists twice, once as skills/<prefix>-<name>/SKILL.md and once as <domain>-skills/<name>/SKILL.md (698 SKILL.md, 349 distinct skills); only the skills/ copy is on the plugin manifest's declared skills path.

Batch 3 anchor and the corpus's first CATEGORY-NESTED layout: 137 skills live at skills/<category>/<skill>/SKILL.md across 17 category directories, one level deeper than every prior target. listSkillDirs only reads immediate subdirs of skills/, so the gate discovers zero skills here and grades the whole library vacuously (sensor reading 21). Grade a single category with --subpath skills/<category> to reach the skills at all.
